summary: Hybrid cloud + on-premises integration: React (Vite SPA) (web) on .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core with Azure SQL Database, hosted on Azure App Service — Central India (Pune), at an estimated $46-276/month.

frontend.justification: Rich interactive screens for an internal tool; team already writes javascript for the UI; internal app behind login needs no SEO; good fast delivery (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 5/5).

alternatives.why_not: With priorities.time_to_market=5, React is faster to deliver with; it fits better: rich interactive screens for an internal tool (project.type=internal_tool).
With priorities.time_to_market=5, React is faster to deliver with.

tradeoffs: The first load waits for the JavaScript bundle, so page weight matters on slow devices
frontend.contrast: React (Vite SPA) (web) rather than Blazor (ASP.NET Core 10). With priorities.time_to_market=5, React is faster to deliver with; it fits better: rich interactive screens for an internal tool (project.type=internal_tool). Trade-off accepted: The first load waits for the JavaScript bundle, so page weight matters on slow devices.

backend.justification: Team already writes csharp for the API; first-class SQL Server driver/ORM; mature security/audit tooling; good maintainability (priority 5/5); good security (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core fits better: first-class SQL Server driver/ORM (infrastructure.existing_systems); with priorities.security=4, it is stronger on security. Known limit of Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS: more boilerplate than Express.

alternatives.choice: Node.js 24 LTS: Next.js route handlers + server actions (same app as the UI)
alternatives.why_not: With priorities.maintainability=5, .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core is easier to maintain; weaker SQL Server tooling (infrastructure.existing_systems).

tradeoffs: Smaller data-science and AI library ecosystem than Python

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: stability 1.00 (robust) over 52 priority vectors; score margin 9.2 over the runner-up.

backend.contrast: .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core rather than Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript). .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core fits better: first-class SQL Server driver/ORM (infrastructure.existing_systems); with priorities.security=4, it is stronger on security. Trade-off accepted: Smaller data-science and AI library ecosystem than Python.

database.choice: Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) — Central India (Pune)
database.justification: Matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs; EF Core + SQL Server is the default .NET pairing; team knows SQL; good maintainability (priority 5/5); good security (priority 4/5). New application data lives in the cloud database; the on-prem server is integrated, not migrated (see supporting 'other').

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17
alternatives.why_not: Azure SQL Database fits better: matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs (infrastructure.existing_systems); EF Core + SQL Server is the default .NET pairing (team.languages=csharp,javascript,sql).

alternatives.choice: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server 8.4
alternatives.why_not: Azure SQL Database fits better: matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs (infrastructure.existing_systems); with priorities.maintainability=5, it is easier to maintain. Known limit of Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server 8.4: 8.0 moved to Sustaining Support (Apr 2026); no row-level security.

tradeoffs: T-SQL and SQL Server features do not port to other engines without rewriting queries; licence cost applies outside Azure SQL

dominated_by: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17
pareto.note: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17 rates at least as well on every priority and better on cost; this choice wins on project fit: matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs; EF Core + SQL Server is the default .NET pairing.

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: stability 1.00 (robust) over 52 priority vectors; score margin 6.7 over the runner-up.

database.contrast: Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) rather than Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server 17. Azure SQL Database fits better: matches the existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 the team already runs (infrastructure.existing_systems); EF Core + SQL Server is the default .NET pairing (team.languages=csharp,javascript,sql). Trade-off accepted: T-SQL and SQL Server features do not port to other engines without rewriting queries; licence cost applies outside Azure SQL.

hosting.choice: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1) — Central India (Pune)
hosting.justification: Hybrid Connections reach the existing on-prem database without opening inbound ports; built-in Entra ID sign-in (Easy Auth); fully managed runtime (patching, TLS, scaling handled) for a team without a DevOps person; good maintainability (priority 5/5); good fast delivery (priority 5/5). Satisfies the hard constraints (cloud_preference azure, managed_cloud (no servers to patch), data_residency india -> Central India (Pune)).

alternatives.why_not: With priorities.maintainability=5 and priorities.time_to_market=5, Azure App Service is easier to maintain and faster to deliver with.
Excluded: infrastructure.cloud_preference=azure rules out Google Cloud Run (runs on gcp).

tradeoffs: Hybrid Connections limited to 5 per Basic plan
Less control than containers for unusual runtimes

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: stability 1.00 (robust) over 52 priority vectors; score margin 15.7 over the runner-up.

hosting.contrast: Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1) rather than Azure Container Apps. With priorities.maintainability=5 and priorities.time_to_market=5, Azure App Service is easier to maintain and faster to deliver with. Trade-off accepted: Hybrid Connections limited to 5 per Basic plan.

what_would_change.new_choice: AWS Elastic Beanstalk (managed platform on EC2) — ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
Azure Virtual Machine (Docker Compose) — Central India (Pune)

supporting.choice: Microsoft Entra ID (existing tenant) via OpenID Connect
supporting.justification: enterprise_sso is required and 'Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)' already exists: reuse it so employees keep one login; app roles/groups in the token drive approvals and admin rights.

alternatives.why_not: duplicates an identity provider the company already operates
extra hop and a second directory to administer

tradeoffs: Depends on the customer's Entra tenant admins for app registration and consent

supporting.justification: ~20 GB of files in 12 months: uploads (images, documents) go straight from clients to object storage via signed URLs. Private bucket, server-generated signed URLs, encryption with managed keys.

alternatives.why_not: with ~20 GB of data expected in 12 months (scale.data_volume_gb_12_months), files inside the database bloat every backup and cost more per GB than object storage
zero egress fees, but a second vendor outside Azure

supporting.justification: .NET 10 LTS + ASP.NET Core tests run on every push and a passing build deploys to Azure App Service; the cost band reserves $0-4/month for a team of 2 (planning estimate).

alternatives.why_not: equally capable; for a team of 2 without a DevOps engineer (team.has_devops=false), ready-made GitHub deploy actions for Azure App Service mean less pipeline code to maintain

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune)
supporting.justification: The 800 ms p95 target and the 99.9% availability target are watched by latency and error-rate alerts; logs and metrics stay with Azure in Central India (Pune), so there is no second vendor.

alternatives.why_not: stores data only in the US or EU

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.choice: Microsoft Graph notifications (Outlook mail / Teams) for approvals
supporting.justification: Approval requests and decisions reach managers in the Microsoft 365 tools they already use, authorised through the existing Entra tenant.

alternatives.why_not: duplicates mail infrastructure the company already has

tradeoffs: Needs admin consent for Graph application permissions

supporting.choice: Integration with existing On-prem SQL Server 2019 via App Service Hybrid Connection (outbound 443 relay, no inbound ports)
supporting.justification: Leave it running as it is and read the data the new application needs through a narrow data-access layer or read API; new tables go in the new database, not in the existing server. The new application keeps its own tables in Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose) and reads the existing data through App Service Hybrid Connection (outbound 443 relay, no inbound ports). A second database exists only because infrastructure.existing_systems lists it without saying it must stay or be retired, so it is left untouched (SQL Server is also the engine of the new database; the new tables are a separate database); if the existing database must stay as the only database, say so in infrastructure.existing_systems, and to migrate off it, say it will be retired.

alternatives.choice: Migrate everything into the new database now
alternatives.why_not: risky in the MVP timeline and breaks existing consumers

alternatives.choice: Use the on-prem server as the only database
alternatives.why_not: ties availability of the new app to the on-prem server and the relay

tradeoffs: Cross-network latency on queries to the on-prem server
Credentials for the on-prem database must live in a secret store

assumptions: Hosting Azure App Service (Linux, Basic B2 / Standard S1): $25-150/month at the 'small' tier.

Database Azure SQL Database (serverless/General Purpose): $15-80/month. Assumes serverless auto-pause outside working hours: about 26-139 active vCore-hours a month at ~$0.57/vCore-hour (Central India rate, 11 Nov 2026); a 0.5-vCore minimum that never pauses is about $210/month compute, and DTU Standard S0 (~$17/month) is the fixed-price alternative.
observability: Azure Monitor + Application Insights in Central India (Pune) $5-30/month.

Stored data ~20 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month: $0-2/month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average); bulk files and media are assumed to sit in object storage, while database rows stay small.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: CDN not added: project.type is internal_tool and the description says it is used only by employees, so a known staff audience is served from one region. Add it when public pages, public media or users on several continents appear.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certifies your organisation's ISMS, not a cloud provider's badge: keep asset inventory, access reviews, logging and change management for this system.
'On-prem SQL Server 2019' is in extended (security-only) support until 2030-01-09; supported, but plan the upgrade path.

assumptions: Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'small' from 1,500 users and ~300 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
